description:
Move the lease checks of bulk update and the CLI dependency edits into their publishing session, classify `dep add` and `dep rm` claims-first, and state in the adopter docs which writes the lease rule covers.

## Background

- Bulk update builds its requests with `enforce_lease: false` (`CapturedFieldUpdate::bulk`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) and checks its matched issues through `refuse_foreign_leases` before its session opens (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`), outside the claims lock.
- `jit dep add` and `jit dep rm` publish the batch variants `CapturedDependencyMutation::Batch` and `RemoveBatch` (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs`), which check the dependent issue through `refuse_foreign_lease` before the session opens; only the single variants check inside the session under a claims guard. `DepCommands::coordinates_claims_first` (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs`) classifies both verbs repository-first; `CLAIM_FIRST_LEAF_COMMANDS` and its inventory test pin the classification.
- The in-session form is `refuse_foreign_leases_held` (`commands/mod.rs`) with a `claims_mutation_guard` taken before the session. A write refuses only when another agent holds an active lease on its target; an unleased issue has nothing to refuse (17fbcf25). Strict refusals downcast to `ForeignLeaseError` (`foreign-lease-error`).
- System-derived writes (readiness corrections of dependents, validate repairs, archive, recovery) are not user requests for the issues they touch.
- `docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/claim.md` say lease enforcement covers "structural issue operations" and "selected write commands" without saying which.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Bulk update checks each matched issue it changes through `refuse_foreign_leases_held` inside its publishing session, holding the claims guard taken before it, and no longer calls the read form; in strict mode an issue under another agent's lease is reported in `errors` and the others still apply, and in warn mode the warning is reported for that issue.
- [hard] REQ-02: `dep add` and `dep rm` check the dependent issue's lease the same way inside their publishing session and no longer call the read form, and both are classified claims-first in the classification and its inventory test.
- [hard] REQ-03: Harness tests show strict mode refusing a bulk update and a `dep add` on another agent's lease with an error that downcasts to `ForeignLeaseError`, the same writes on an unleased issue succeeding, and no lease check for readiness corrections of dependents.
- [hard] REQ-04: The configuration and claim references state the lease-checked writes as a rule (every user-requested write to an existing issue refuses when another agent holds an active lease on an issue it targets, including bulk update, `dep add`/`dep rm`, assign, unassign, template application and the gate commands; system-derived writes check nothing) rather than a hand-kept command list, and no other page restates it (`@/charter/D-13`).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: bulk update and `dep add`/`dep rm` read leases under the claims lock, and the two dependency verbs lock claims before the repository; which writes refuse is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; locate symbols by name.
title: Bulk and dependency edits check leases in their publishing session
